name: Midtown
tagline: High-rise core with Piedmont Park at the door
description: Atlanta's densest walkable district, a wall of glass towers along Peachtree Street backed by Piedmont Park, the Botanical Garden and Georgia Tech. Tech offices, museums and restaurants fill the ground floors. Nearly every building is a rental high-rise with a gym, pool and coworking lounge, and four MARTA stations serve it.
bestFor: Remote workers who want a doorman building, a gym downstairs and no car
pros: Best walkability and MARTA access in the city
Piedmont Park and the BeltLine for running
High-rise rentals with in-building work lounges
cons: Among the highest rents in Atlanta
Feels corporate and transient rather than neighbourly

name: Old Fourth Ward
tagline: BeltLine, Ponce City Market and the best cafe density
description: The stretch between downtown and Inman Park, transformed by the Eastside BeltLine trail and the redeveloped Ponce City Market food hall. Brick warehouses, new mid-rise apartments and the Krog Street tunnel murals define it. You can run, eat and work along the trail without ever crossing a road.
bestFor: Nomads who want BeltLine access, food halls and coworking within a walk
pros: Directly on the Eastside BeltLine trail
Ponce City Market plus dozens of independent cafes
Historic Fourth Ward Park and a skatepark on the doorstep
cons: Rents have risen sharply, little is cheap now
BeltLine crowds and bar noise on weekend nights
Car break-ins in street parking are common

name: West Midtown
tagline: Warehouse conversions, design shops and big restaurants
description: Old industrial blocks along Howell Mill and Marietta Street reworked into loft apartments, furniture showrooms, breweries and some of Atlanta's most ambitious restaurants. It sits next to Georgia Tech. Loft ceilings, parking included and slightly softer rents than Midtown make it a solid long-stay base.
bestFor: Nomads who want loft space and serious restaurants, and do not mind driving
pros: Slightly cheaper than Midtown for more space
cons: No MARTA rail, you effectively need a car
Howell Mill traffic is bad most of the day
Few everyday shops between the destination spots

name: Grant Park
tagline: Victorian streets around the city's oldest park
description: A quiet intown neighbourhood of restored Victorian and craftsman homes on shaded streets, wrapped around the 131-acre park and Zoo Atlanta. The Beacon development and a Sunday farmers market anchor it. Calm enough for all-day calls while still being three miles from downtown.
bestFor: Nomads who want a peaceful residential street and a park, still close to the centre
pros: Big park, farmers market and genuine neighbourhood feel
Quiet streets, good for focused work
Southside BeltLine access is improving fast
cons: Thin cafe and restaurant options within walking distance
No MARTA rail station, car or bus needed
Older houses often mean weak insulation and old wiring

name: East Atlanta Village
tagline: Dive bars, cheap rents and the scrappiest intown scene
description: A small crossroads of dive bars, live music rooms, taco spots and vintage shops surrounded by bungalow streets southeast of the centre. It is the least polished intown option and the cheapest. Musicians, artists and younger renters keep it lively without the BeltLine price premium.
bestFor: Budget nomads who want intown nightlife and a bungalow rental at a fair price
pros: Cheapest rents of the popular intown neighbourhoods
Compact walkable village of bars and live music
Bungalows with yards instead of apartment boxes
cons: Property crime rates are higher than in Midtown
Bar noise late on weekends near the village
Poor transit, you will need a car for most trips
